patch.value: password_assignment treats any value starting with a ${...} or $(...) reference as a placeholder, so a literal concatenated with a reference passes the guard

Reported 2026-11-10 by the fleet session from pm-memory#51's latest review (also commented on GH-1699). The flat value grammar in src/core/shared/secret-rules.ts (PASSWORD_VALUE) excludes every value whose first characters are '<', '${' or '$(' via a negative lookahead. A credential written as a literal next to an environment reference is therefore never judged: password=${EMPTY}"<literal>", password=$VAR"<literal>" and password=<literal>${VAR} pass both the SDK mutation guard and the repository scan. When the reference expands to nothing, the literal is the credential. A bare reference (password=${BUILD_PASSWORD}) must stay allowed, so a value is a placeholder only when the reference is the whole value. The structured pass added by pm-gh1699 inherits the same grammar, so quoted-key spellings behave the same way. This changes the flat rule, which also feeds the repository scan, so the change needs a repository-wide false-positive check like pm-gh1699's. Duplicate check: searched 'password placeholder reference concatenated literal env'. The pm-gh1699 must-allow corpus only covers whole-value references.

Must refuse in both consumers: a literal after a ${...} reference, after a $VAR reference, and before a ${...} reference, in flat and quoted-key spellings; Must allow in both consumers: a bare ${BUILD_PASSWORD}, a bare $(op read pw), a bare <placeholder> and an empty fallback; node scripts/check-secrets.mjs stays clean over every tracked file and the linear-time control still passes

A literal concatenated with an environment or command reference is judged as a credential, while a value that is only a reference stays allowed, in both the flat and structured spellings and in both consumers.

value.text: Implementation (branch fix/secret-guard-grammar-and-payload-keys): PASSWORD_VALUE now captures the whole value, and the rule declares minimumLiteralLength: 8, which acceptsSecretMatch applies to literalAfterReferences(match[1]). That helper expands run-time references to nothing (${NAME}, ${NAME:?message}, $(command), <placeholder>), keeps the default of ${NAME:-word} / ${NAME:=word} as literal text, and then removes the delimiting quotes of each quoted piece. A value that starts with a quote is that quoted literal alone (JSON and YAML semantics); an unquoted value is a run of references and literal characters that may hold one whitespace-free quoted piece, as a shell concatenates $VAR"literal". Two design corrections came from running the gates: (1) letting a quoted piece concatenate freely made a value spill across later JSON keys and flagged 39,999 keys of the existing pathological-input test, so a quoted start is now the literal alone and only one inner piece is allowed, which also keeps the structured pass linear; (2) the repository scan flagged tests/unit/core/sentry/instrument.spec.ts, where the quote after password=<private-value> closes the enclosing JS string, so the inner piece must be whitespace-free. Element content (<password>...</password>) now uses the same literal judgment, so <password>${X}literal</password> is refused and <password>${X}</password> stays clean. Must-refuse and must-allow tables run through both consumers (scripts/check-secrets-lib.mjs scanContent and scanMutationSecrets). node scripts/check-secrets.mjs is clean over every tracked file, and the existing GH-1699 and GH-1704 specs (227 tests) pass unchanged. Behavior kept on purpose: a bare $VAR reference is still read as literal text, as before, because the acceptance criteria name only ${...}, $(...), <...> and empty fallbacks as must-allow.

value.text: Codex review round 1 (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) found five password-grammar gaps, all fixed: (1) password="${EMPTY}"<literal> and [sample: a literal split over two quoted pieces] were missed because a value starting with a quote was that literal alone and only one quoted piece was allowed; a value may now hold up to four whitespace-free quoted pieces, including a quoted start, which keeps each scan bounded to a few later keys (two existing linear-time inputs now read as concatenated literals, and their pinned counts were updated with a comment: '"password":"' x 40,000 and '"password"=a"x"' x 40,000 each report 39,999 keys, still linear); (2) nested references were false positives (${PRIMARY:-${SECONDARY}}, a quoted $(op read $(cat name))) because two non-nesting regex replacements ran in sequence; literalAfterReferences now uses expandRuntimeReferences, a single linear pass with a frame stack, and the regex accepts one nesting level; (3) [sample: an element body holding an apostrophe] lost an apostrophe because element content went through shell quote removal; element content now only expands references; (4) <password><x>literal</password> never reached the judge because the element body pattern was [^<]*; the body now admits markup and placeholder spans other than tags of the same keys; (5) {"admin-password":"$(op read pw)literal"} was rejected by the prefixed-key whitespace check reading the raw match; for literal-judged rules that check now reads the literal. ${NAME:+word} keeps its word as literal too. Must-refuse and must-allow tables in both consumers cover every case, and node scripts/check-secrets.mjs stays clean (the new spec builds credential-shaped samples at runtime, following the existing convention).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 2 (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh): a quoted closing delimiter inside a command substitution (a printf of a quoted parenthesis followed by eight letters, both unquoted and inside double quotes) ended the reference early. That reported a credential where the whole value is one command reference, which the old detector kept clean. Fixed in both layers. expandRuntimeReferences tracks quote state inside non-default reference frames (quotedStep: a quote opens a span that nothing inside closes, and a backslash escapes the next character in double quotes). The regex PASSWORD_PIECE skips single- and double-quoted spans inside $(...). A default word keeps its quotes as literal text. Not fixed, by decision: references nested three or more levels in an unquoted value. The declared regex grammar follows one nesting level; deeper nesting is followed inside quoted values and elements. This is documented in docs/MUTATION_INTEGRITY.md and recorded as a residual on pm-jcz7qz. Two credential-shaped samples that review comments on this item had quoted verbatim were removed with pm history-redact (audited, chain verified) after the repository scan flagged them under the new grammar.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 3 (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) found three password false positives against the merge base, all fixed. (1) A quoted closing brace inside a required-variable reference ended the braced reference early in the regex. The braced-reference piece now skips single- and double-quoted spans, as the command-substitution piece does (PASSWORD_QUOTED_SPAN). (2) Escaped quoted values were judged after decodeQuotedLiteral neutralized their own quote characters, so a double-quoted printf inside a command substitution in a JSON string read as single-quoted and closed early. decodeQuotedLiteral now returns the neutralized reading for the value grammar and the decoded original at the same length. The value regex is compiled with the d flag, and valueMatch judges the original span of capture 1. For credential_key_assignment this also measures entropy on the decoded original, which is pm-jcz7qz's second criterion for escaped literals. (3) A literal dollar sign could consume the opener of a reference the grammar cannot follow (one nested three levels deep), adding one literal character to seven. A literal $ now never consumes a following { or (. The walker also tracks quotes in every reference frame: a default word keeps its quoted text with its quotes for the later quote removal, and inside double quotes a nested reference still opens, as in the shell. The must-allow table gained each case; samples are built at runtime.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: PR 1745 bot review (first head b9458c03b), all fixed in b4374fe3b. (1) CodeQL js/polynomial-redos alert 58 flagged the sticky NAME:- prefix pattern used by openReference. It is replaced by defaultedPrefixLength, a single forward scan. (2) Greptile (P1) and CodeRabbit (Major) found the same regression against main. After the round-3 change, an escaped value was judged on its decoded original, but literalAfterReferences then treated the decoded quote characters as shell delimiters, so an eight-character password whose only escape is an escaped double quote measured seven and was missed. A decoded literal's own delimiters are now syntax and every decoded character between them is data. valueMatch clamps capture 1 to the decoded body and marks the match, and judgedLiteral expands only references for marked matches. (3) CodeRabbit (Minor): an escaped closing parenthesis inside an unquoted command substitution ended it early. A backslash now escapes the next character outside quotes and in double quotes inside any reference, in both quotedStep and the regex pieces. Single quotes keep a backslash literal. (4) Gates (static) failed at pnpm security:scan on this branch's own pm-hw00c2 filing description, which quoted a password assignment to a bare shell variable. The earlier local scans were clean only because the new item files were not yet tracked; check-secrets reads git ls-files. The description was reworded and the literal removed with pm history-redact. Hosted coverage on b9458c03b also reported the scalarFinds escaped-and-direct and compact branches and the new Set dedupe as uncovered. Each now has a regression case, and a targeted coverage run reports both source files fully covered.

Up to four whitespace-free quoted pieces concatenate; element bodies admit markup spans; escaped values are judged on their decoded data; three Codex rounds and the PR bots drove the final grammar

Must-refuse and must-allow tables pass in both consumers, check-secrets is clean over every tracked file, and hosted Gates (coverage) and Gates (static) pass on PR 1745; unquoted references nested three or more levels remain a documented limit recorded on pm-jcz7qz

value.text: Follow-up after close, from the CodeRabbit review of ed3cbd37b (PR 1745). Fixed: a default word's own quote delimiters counted toward the literal, so a password whose whole value is a reference with a six-character quoted default was reported. The walker now applies the shell's quote removal inside a reference word: quote delimiters and escaping backslashes contribute nothing, and the quoted text itself contributes. Both quote kinds are pinned at six (clean) and eight (reported) characters. Declined, with a reason recorded on pm-jcz7qz: an escaped quoted literal followed directly by an unquoted suffix in the same value has only its literal judged. Main has the same behavior, so this is not a regression. Judging the suffix needs a mixed data-and-text literal model; it is in the adversarial corpus residuals.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Follow-up after close, from the Greptile review of 6669889b7 (PR 1745): unquoting default words in the expansion pass made the old second pass (top-level quote removal) strip quotes twice. A double-quoted default holding an apostrophe measured seven, and a backslash before an ordinary letter inside double quotes was dropped although the shell keeps it. Both are fixed by one walker, expandWords, that identifies every delimiter exactly once. Text mode (literalAfterReferences) treats top-level quotes as delimiters; data mode (expandRuntimeReferences, for decoded literals and element bodies) treats them as data. Inside reference words, both modes apply the shell's quote removal, and a backslash in double quotes escapes only $, a backtick, a double quote, a backslash and a line break. Regression cases pin both Greptile samples as text and as payload members, plus the six-character quoted defaults in both quote kinds.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Follow-up after close, from the CodeRabbit review of 839447b1b (PR 1745), both fixed. (1) The element body pattern repeated one alternation per character, so a body of about 16 million characters exhausted the V8 backtrack stack and the guard failed open (main's [^<]* did not). The element spelling now compiles an opening-tag pattern plus sticky closing-tag and markup-span patterns, and elementBodyEnd scans the body in code with indexOf, with the same semantics. The reference walker also appends runs of plain characters at once (PLAIN_RUN), so a 20-million-character body takes about a second. (2) JSON.stringify leaves U+2028 and U+2029 raw, and a raw line break is rejected as a text artifact, so a payload password holding one was never judged. acceptsStructuredValue now escapes both after serialization, which judges them like a line feed.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Follow-up after close, from the Greptile review of 201e65363 (PR 1745), fixed: the plain-run fast path used a sticky regex with the u flag. After an escape consumed the first half of a surrogate pair, a match could start one code unit early, inside the pair, and advancing by its length skipped the next quote. A whole command reference escaping an astral character was then read as unclosed literal text and reported. PLAIN_RUN drops the u flag, so a sticky match starts exactly at lastIndex. Restoring the u flag fails three of the new regression tests.
